name: China
tagline: The joint-venture universities are the real English-taught route
summary: China is two systems for an IB student applying from Denmark: English-taught joint universities, and Chinese universities that teach mostly in Chinese. The Sino-foreign joint universities — NYU Shanghai, Duke Kunshan, XJTLU, Nottingham Ningbo, CUHK-Shenzhen, BNBU and Wenzhou-Kean — teach in English, award a foreign or joint degree and admit on their own or the American calendar. The Chinese universities, such as Tsinghua, Peking and Zhejiang, admit international students by application and review, teach mostly in Chinese, and from 2026/2027 require a new national test, the CSCA, before you apply.
whyConsider: The joint-venture universities give you a fully English-taught degree and, usually, two diplomas: a Chinese one and an American or British one. Duke Kunshan awards both a US and a Chinese degree.
Deadlines work for IB students: Duke Kunshan's Regular Decision deadline is 4 January 2027, with an acceptance deadline of 1 May 2027 — a normal American calendar you can plan around.
Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool offers over 60 English-taught undergraduate programmes with a dual XJTLU and University of Liverpool degree, plus 2+2 and 2+1+1 routes that let you finish in Liverpool.

Chinese Government Scholarships (the CSC scheme) fund bachelor's degrees including tuition, accommodation, a living stipend and medical insurance, applied for through the Chinese embassy or directly through a university.
Tuition and living costs at the domestic universities are low by any international standard, and Mandarin is a genuinely valuable thing to spend four years acquiring.
watchOuts: No official Chinese tuition figure or scholarship amount is quoted here. Deadlines are given for Duke Kunshan, NYU Shanghai and XJTLU; for BNBU (2025 entry) and Zhejiang (2026) only last cycle's dates are published; ask the others directly.

From the 2026/2027 academic year, anyone applying for a bachelor's degree at a Chinese university must sit the CSCA (来华留学本科入学学业水平测试) before applying. It runs five times a year — January, March, April, June and December — and registration is at csca.cn. Ask the joint universities whether they require it.

Peking University's Yenching Academy is a one-year master's programme, not an undergraduate route. Yuanpei College is PKU's liberal-arts honours college but teaches principally in Chinese. Neither is an English-taught bachelor's entry point.

At the domestic universities, 'international undergraduate admission' usually assumes HSK Chinese proficiency — typically HSK 4 to 6 depending on the programme — or a year of preparatory Chinese language study first. Do not assume English-taught.
Joint-venture tuition is high by Chinese standards: NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan charge near-American fees, though both offer substantial scholarships and need-based aid.

Political and academic conditions differ sharply from Europe. Internet access is restricted, academic freedom on certain topics is limited, and your ability to research some subjects will be constrained. Think about whether your intended field is affected.
Visa, residence permit and annual health-check requirements are administratively heavy, and rules change with relatively little notice.
If you can claim Danish SU, it works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA: check su.dk before budgeting. If you cannot, check your own country's student finance.

ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion. The joint-venture universities apply their Western parent's IB requirements; the domestic universities read the transcript within their own international admissions process.
notes: At the joint-venture universities the IB is standard currency and is read exactly as it would be by the parent institution in the US or UK.

At the Chinese universities, the IB satisfies the secondary-education requirement, but admission also turns on the CSCA (required from 2026/2027), Chinese proficiency (HSK) for Chinese-taught programmes, and sometimes an interview.
Duke Kunshan operates a test-optional policy for standardised tests; it publishes no IB score requirement on its admissions pages.
The one IB score published: XJTLU asks for an IB Diploma with 30 points for international students entering Year Two. No other Chinese institution on this page publishes a minimum.

portal.name: No central portal, and no replacement for the one that has gone. Campus China (China Scholarship Council) was the official information and scholarship site and its domain no longer resolves; joint-venture universities use the Common Application or their own portals, and the Chinese universities publish inside login-gated application systems of their own.

deadlines.label: There is no Chinese national admissions deadline for an international applicant, and the two intakes are not one cycle
deadlines.notes: China has no UCAS, no Common App and no ministry-run deadline for international undergraduates. The gaokao, which is the national examination the whole Chinese calendar bends around, is not a route an international IB candidate takes at all; international applicants are admitted by each university under its own 申请-审核 (application and review) procedure, on its own dates. Two things follow that the rest of this page depends on. First, every date below belongs to one institution and nothing generalises from it. Second, China runs two intakes — a September one, which is the main one and the one this page covers, and a separate February or March spring intake which a smaller number of programmes offer. "2027 entry" on this page means September 2027 unless an entry says otherwise, and a deadline you find on a Chinese university's site may belong to the spring intake and be eight months out of step with the one you want. Check which intake a date is for before you plan around it. Note also that China's joint-venture universities — Duke Kunshan, NYU Shanghai, Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool, Nottingham Ningbo, CUHK-Shenzhen, United International College, Wenzhou-Kean — run on an entirely different calendar from Tsinghua, Peking, Fudan and Shanghai Jiao Tong, and several run on the American one.

deadlines.label: Duke Kunshan University — Early Decision, and it is binding
deadlines.audience: international applicants — DKU states these must be non-Chinese citizens
deadlines.notes: Published with its full calendar year on DKU's English international-admissions site as "Early decision application deadline: November 2, 2026 (11:59pm ET)", which is 05:59 on 3 November in Denmark. Applications are made through the Common App, which DKU began accepting for the 2027 entry term in August 2026, and Early Decision on the Common App is binding: you may hold one Early Decision application only, and if admitted you withdraw the rest and enrol. DKU's own How to Apply page does not restate those terms, so the binding force comes from the Common App agreement you sign rather than from anything DKU publishes — read it before you file. There is no application fee. The CSS Profile is required if you are seeking financial aid, and DKU is test-optional for the 2026-2027 cycle. A warning that matters more than any of this: DKU runs two entirely separate admissions tracks on the same domain. The Chinese-language site (admissions.dukekunshan.edu.cn, 中文 – 中国学生) publishes a 综合评价 comprehensive-evaluation route with rounds closing 3 January and 5 February, for Chinese students. Those are not your dates. An international applicant uses the English site marked "English – International Students", and DKU states that international applicants must be non-Chinese citizens.

deadlines.label: NYU Shanghai — Early Decision I, and it is binding
deadlines.notes: NYU Shanghai publishes "November 1" and "11:59 p.m EST" with no calendar year, so 2026 is expected rather than confirmed. It is binding, and NYU's wording is more specific than most: if you are admitted to the campus you named as your primary interest, "you must accept the offer within 25 days", and "If accepted, you'll also need to withdraw applications from other schools, and cannot submit new applications" — so an NYU Shanghai Early Decision admission in December ends your application season, including applications you have already paid for elsewhere. One Common Application covers all three of NYU's degree-granting campuses, New York, Abu Dhabi and Shanghai, which is why an Early Decision here binds you against the others. The application fee is US$85, with waivers available.

deadlines.label: NYU Shanghai — Early Decision II, also binding
deadlines.notes: Published as "January 1" with no calendar year, so 2027 is expected rather than confirmed. Same binding terms as Early Decision I, in the same window as Regular Decision, and it exists for a student whose first binding choice turned them down in December. The 25-day acceptance rule and the requirement to withdraw every other application apply here too.

deadlines.label: Duke Kunshan University — Regular Decision
deadlines.audience: international applicants — DKU states these must be non-Chinese citizens
deadlines.notes: Published with its full calendar year as "Regular decision application deadline: January 4, 2027 (11:59pm ET)", which is 05:59 on 5 January in Denmark. Not binding: you keep every offer you hold and reply on 1 May 2027, which is its own entry below. The DKU application is the Common App plus two DKU-specific essays, and DKU also lets an applicant to Duke University in North Carolina share that application with DKU — but only the materials submitted at that moment are shared, and transcripts, school reports, recommendations and CSS Profile documents that arrive later must be sent to both universities separately. That is the detail most likely to cost somebody an assessed application.

deadlines.label: NYU Shanghai — Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Published on NYU Shanghai's How to Apply page as "Regular Decision - January 5", 11:59 p.m. EST, with no calendar year, so 2027 is expected rather than confirmed. The Early Decision page leaves it out.

deadlines.label: Duke Kunshan University — Regular Decision acceptance deadline
deadlines.audience: applicants holding a Duke Kunshan Regular Decision offer
deadlines.notes: Published on DKU's international-admissions homepage with its year as "May 1, 2027 (11:59 PM ET) — Regular Decision Acceptance Deadline". It is the same day as the American national candidates' reply date, which is no coincidence: DKU recruits against American colleges through the Common App and keeps their calendar. It falls more than two months before IB results are released, so the offer you accept is conditional on predicted grades, and what DKU does if your final results fall short is not published. Ask before you accept. An Early Decision admission does not get this date; that choice was made in November.

deadlines.label: Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University — applications close for most programmes
deadlines.notes: XJTLU states "the closing date for September 2027 entry is 31 May 2027" for most undergraduate programmes. International students with the IB are considered for Year Two entry with 30 points; admitted students pay a non-refundable RMB 10,000 deposit towards tuition.

deadlines.label: Tsinghua University — international undergraduate admission, in three batches whose dates are behind a login
deadlines.audience: international applicants — Tsinghua requires a foreign passport, and foreign permanent residency does not qualify
deadlines.notes: Tsinghua admits international undergraduates under 申请-审核, application and review, in three application batches. The batches take the same form and the same documents but have different application periods, different interview dates and different result dates, and applicants to the Design (设计学类) and Fine Arts (美术学类) programmes must apply in the first batch — so for those two, the earliest batch is the only batch. The dates themselves are not published on any open page: they live inside the online application system at apply.join-tsinghua.edu.cn, which requires an account before anything can be seen, and one email address may be registered only once per year. That is why this entry has no date. Two facts from Tsinghua's own Chinese-language applicant FAQ matter more than any date: Tsinghua's undergraduate teaching is in Chinese (部分课程采用双语或英语教学 — some courses are bilingual or in English) with international students generally in the same classes as Chinese students, and the language requirement is HSK level 5 with at least 60 in every section, or HSK 4 on entry with HSK 5 to be reached within a year of enrolling or the place is withdrawn. Clinical Medicine does not take international undergraduates and Tsinghua accepts no transfer students. That FAQ is in Chinese only, has no English equivalent, and is dated to the 2017 cycle — so its structure is worth knowing and none of its numbers should be trusted for 2027. Confirm everything with admissions@tsinghua.edu.cn before building a plan on it.

deadlines.label: Peking University, Fudan University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University — international undergraduate admission
deadlines.notes: Dates not confirmed here. Each of the three runs its own application-and-review procedure on its own calendar, and they will not agree. The shape to expect, from Tsinghua and from Zhejiang's 2026 guide (1 December 2025 to 28 February 2026, with some majors open until 31 May 2026): windows opening in the late autumn and closing between winter and early spring for a September intake, often published only inside a login-gated application system, and a CSCA score required before you apply from 2026/2027. Read each university's own international-student admissions page (留学生本科招生) in Chinese; the English pages are consistently thinner.

deadlines.label: Chinese Government Scholarship (CGS/CSC): each embassy and university sets its own date
deadlines.notes: The Chinese Government Scholarship is applied for by one of three routes with three different calendars: Type A through the Chinese embassy in your country of citizenship, Type B directly to a CSC-designated Chinese university, and Type C through certain international organisations. Each embassy and each university sets its own closing date, so there is no single deadline. www.campuschina.org, the China Scholarship Council portal that embassy notices still name, did not resolve on 23 or 24 September 2026, and the Chinese Embassy in Denmark's English site (the Type A channel for Danish citizens) carried no scholarship notice on either day. From October 2026, watch the announcements of the Chinese embassy in your country of citizenship for the 2027/2028 notice and ask each university for its Type B date.

deadlines.label: IB results released
deadlines.notes: Listed because of where it sits rather than because anything in China is waiting for it. Every date on this page that has been established falls before it: Duke Kunshan closes Regular Decision in January and wants your acceptance on 1 May, and NYU Shanghai's binding early rounds are decided in December. So a Chinese joint-venture offer, like an American one, is made on predicted grades and accepted before you have real ones, and what happens if the results fall short is set by each university and is not established here. The Chinese universities' own timing is unknown for the same reason their deadlines are. The date is the IB's usual results day and is not yet confirmed by the IB for 2027.

steps: Decide first whether you want a Mandarin-medium education with a preparatory language year, or an English-medium joint-venture degree. They are different projects with different calendars.
For the joint-venture universities, work to the American calendar: shortlist in September 2026, apply by early November for Early Decision or early January for Regular Decision.
For a domestic university, check the HSK Chinese requirement for your intended programme before anything else, and budget for a preparatory year if you do not have it.
If you want a Chinese Government Scholarship, decide early between the embassy route and the university route — you normally cannot use both, and the embassy route closes earlier.
Prepare the standard international pack: IB transcript and predicted grades, personal statement, references, passport copy, a physical examination record, and a non-criminal record certificate.
Once admitted, the university issues a JW201 or JW202 form and an admission notice; you apply for an X1 student visa at the Chinese embassy in Copenhagen.
Within 30 days of arrival, convert the X1 visa into a residence permit at the local Public Security Bureau and complete the medical examination.
application.selectionNotes: NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan are selective on the American model — essays, references, interviews, holistic review — and both admit small cohorts split between Chinese and international students. XJTLU, Nottingham Ningbo and CUHK-Shenzhen apply their parent university's published requirements and are more predictable. Tsinghua and Peking are highly selective even in the international pool.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Concentrated in the joint-venture universities. XJTLU alone lists over 60 English-taught undergraduate programmes; NYU Shanghai, Duke Kunshan, Nottingham Ningbo, CUHK-Shenzhen and Wenzhou-Kean teach entirely in English. The domestic elite universities offer only a handful, mostly in economics, international relations and Chinese studies.
language.englishProof: Set per university. XJTLU wants IELTS 6.5 (5.5 in each section) or TOEFL iBT 90 for Year Two entry; NYU Shanghai requires an English test from non-native speakers unless the last three years of school were taught in English; Duke Kunshan encourages but does not require one. Ask whether IB English counts in place of a test.
notes: At the joint-venture universities you do not need Mandarin to enrol, but all of them require you to study it, and NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan build Chinese language into the degree.

At the domestic universities, HSK 4 to 6 is the normal requirement for a Chinese-taught degree. Many international students spend a funded preparatory year reaching it — the Chinese Government Scholarship includes this.
Four years of immersion is a fast route to genuine working Mandarin, and a strong non-academic argument for studying in China.

tuitionEuEea.value: China does not differentiate by EU status. International students pay an international rate at domestic universities; joint-venture universities charge a single fee to everyone.

costs.applicationFee: Charged by each university: Duke Kunshan none; NYU Shanghai US$85 (waivers available). XJTLU takes a non-refundable RMB 10,000 deposit towards tuition from admitted students.
notes: No official Chinese tuition figure is quoted here; ask each university for its fees.

The structure to expect: domestic universities charge an international-student tuition rate per year that is low by Western standards, plus accommodation in a designated international dormitory. Joint-venture universities charge considerably more — NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan approach American levels, XJTLU and Nottingham Ningbo sit in between.
Living costs in Beijing and Shanghai are moderate by European standards; Suzhou, Ningbo, Kunshan and Zhuhai are considerably cheaper.
Most universities require international students to buy a specified Chinese medical insurance policy as a condition of registration — budget for it separately.

funding: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC), administered by the China Scholarship Council — the main government scheme, covering bachelor's degrees. Two routes: Type A through the Chinese embassy in Copenhagen, and Type B directly through a participating university. It normally covers tuition, on-campus accommodation, a monthly living stipend and comprehensive medical insurance, and can include a preparatory Chinese language year. Confirm the amounts with the embassy.
Confucius Institute Scholarships fund Chinese language and teaching-related degrees specifically.
Provincial and municipal government scholarships (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) are separate schemes with their own applications, often administered by the university.
Duke Kunshan offers merit scholarships, need-based financial aid and a named Duke Kunshan University Full Scholarship. Ask DKU for the terms.
NYU Shanghai offers scholarships and financial aid to international students; ask it for details.
XJTLU and Nottingham Ningbo run entrance scholarships based on academic performance at admission.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

workRights: Students on a residence permit for study may take part-time work or internships only with the explicit endorsement of both the university and the exit-entry administration, recorded on the residence permit. The rules are restrictive; confirm them with the university. Do not plan to fund yourself by working.
residency: EU citizenship gives no shortcut. Once admitted you receive an admission notice and a JW201 (scholarship students) or JW202 (self-funded) form, which you take to the Chinese embassy in Copenhagen for an X1 visa. Within 30 days of arrival you must convert it into a residence permit at the local Public Security Bureau, which requires a medical examination at a designated Chinese facility — a foreign medical certificate is usually not accepted. The permit is renewed annually.
housing: Domestic universities house international students in designated international student dormitories on or near campus, which is the standard arrangement and is cheap. The joint-venture universities house undergraduates in modern residence halls — Duke Kunshan and NYU Shanghai both operate residential campuses. Renting privately as a foreign student is possible but involves police registration of your address within 24 hours of moving.
healthcare: International students are normally required to buy a specified Chinese medical insurance policy as a condition of registration, and to pass a medical examination as part of the residence permit process. Public hospitals are inexpensive but crowded; international clinics in Beijing and Shanghai are good and expensive. Your EHIC does not apply.

institutions.name: Tsinghua University
institutions.englishBachelors: No fully English-taught bachelor's is listed. Tsinghua's applicant FAQ says undergraduate teaching is in Chinese, with some courses bilingual or in English, and asks for HSK 5 (or HSK 4 on entry and HSK 5 within a year).
institutions.note: Admits international undergraduates through a separate process, but teaches mainly in Chinese. For a student without Chinese it is realistically a Mandarin destination after a preparatory year.

institutions.name: Peking University
institutions.englishBachelors: Very limited. Yuanpei College is PKU's liberal-arts honours college but teaches principally in Chinese. The Yenching Academy is a one-year master's programme, not an undergraduate route. Most international undergraduates study in Mandarin.
institutions.note: A university on a classical lakeside campus in Beijing. Be clear about what is on offer: Yenching is postgraduate and Yuanpei is Chinese-medium, so PKU is realistically a Mandarin-language destination.

institutions.name: Fudan University
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number of English-taught bachelor's programmes, historically including clinical medicine (MBBS) and some economics and international relations tracks. Verify directly.
institutions.note: A comprehensive university in Shanghai, strong in the humanities and social sciences. Its English-taught MBBS is a well-known English-medium medical degree.

institutions.name: Shanghai Jiao Tong University
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited. Some English-taught tracks exist in engineering and medicine; the SJTU-ParisTech Elite Institute of Technology teaches in French and Chinese. Verify directly.
institutions.note: A large engineering-led university in Shanghai, and the institution that created the Academic Ranking of World Universities. Its joint institutes with Michigan and with ParisTech are the most internationally accessible parts.

institutions.name: NYU Shanghai
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught entirely in English, across business, data science, computer science, humanities, social science, neuroscience and interactive media arts. Awards an NYU degree and a Chinese degree.
institutions.note: A full NYU campus in Pudong, with students roughly half Chinese and half international from more than 70 countries. Every student studies Mandarin, semesters are available across NYU's global network, and deadlines follow the American calendar via the Common Application.

institutions.name: Duke Kunshan University
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught in English, across a liberal arts and sciences curriculum with interdisciplinary majors. Graduates receive both a US degree and a Chinese degree.
institutions.note: Early Decision closes 2 November 2026 and Regular Decision 4 January 2027, with acceptance by 1 May 2027. It is test-optional, with merit scholarships, need-based aid and a full scholarship, and sits between Shanghai and Suzhou on the high-speed line.

institutions.name: Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University
institutions.englishBachelors: Over 60 undergraduate programmes, all taught in English, across engineering, science, business, humanities, film and design. Graduates receive dual XJTLU and University of Liverpool degrees.
institutions.note: Over 60 English-taught programmes, with a dual XJTLU and Liverpool degree. 2+2 and 2+1+1 routes let you finish in Liverpool, and Suzhou is an hour from Shanghai and much cheaper.

institutions.name: University of Nottingham Ningbo China
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught in English, awarding a University of Nottingham degree. Business, engineering, international studies, education and science.
institutions.note: A Nottingham campus opened in 2004, awarding the same degree as in the UK. You can transfer to the Nottingham or Malaysia campus, and Ningbo is a comfortable port city south of Shanghai.

institutions.name: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught in English, across science and engineering, management and economics, humanities and social science, data science, medicine and music. Awards a CUHK degree.
institutions.note: A full mainland campus of the Hong Kong university, awarding the CUHK degree, in Shenzhen, thirty minutes from Hong Kong. Its international application system is open from September to April.

institutions.name: Beijing Normal-Hong Kong Baptist University
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught entirely in English, in a whole-person liberal arts model: business, culture and creativity, humanities and social science, science and technology.
institutions.note: A joint liberal-arts college founded by Beijing Normal and Hong Kong Baptist universities. Small, English-medium, residential, and in Zhuhai next to Macau — much cheaper than the Shanghai options.

institutions.name: Wenzhou-Kean University
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, taught in English by an American faculty, awarding both a Kean University (New Jersey) degree and a Chinese degree. Business, computer science, architecture, psychology, biology and education.
institutions.note: An American public university's full Chinese campus, awarding the US degree, with small classes and an American curriculum. Considerably cheaper and less selective than NYU Shanghai or Duke Kunshan, and a genuine route to a US qualification.

institutions.name: Zhejiang University
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited at the main university; the ZJU-UoE Institute (with Edinburgh) and ZJU-UIUC Institute (with Illinois) at the Haining International Campus teach in English and award dual degrees.
institutions.note: A large university in Hangzhou, Alibaba's home city. Its International Campus at Haining, with Edinburgh and Illinois, is the English-taught entry point and awards dual degrees.

institutions.name: Tongji University
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number of English-taught bachelor's programmes, historically in civil engineering and architecture. Verify directly.
institutions.note: Founded as a German-Chinese medical school, with Sino-German institutes and exchange routes today. Strong in architecture and civil engineering.

institutions.name: Sun Yat-sen University
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited. Some English-taught medicine and business tracks; most undergraduate teaching is in Mandarin. Verify directly.
institutions.note: A comprehensive university across three Pearl River Delta cities, strong in medicine and marine science. Chinese-medium for most purposes.
